newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes slightly down vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes slightly down vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly down at 8.2926 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Monday from 8.2922 last Friday with no impact seen from a central bank statement that it intends to increase intervention, dealers said.
The weighted average price last Friday was 8.2925.

The Beijing-based Financial Times newspaper last Friday quoted Zhou Xiaochuan, vice-governor of the People's Bank of China, as saying the central bank would step up intervention on the foreign exchange market to prevent the yuan from rising sharply.
Dealers said his comments had no impact on market sentiment and the yuan moved stably in a narrow range between 8.2920 and 8.2930.
The yuan opened little changed at 8.2923 and consolidated around 8.2920 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2918 and a low of 8.2927.
Trading was dull with most done at 8.2922, dealers said.
One dealer said Zhou's comments implied the central bank would depress the yuan if it rose too high.
"Given the yuan's already high level, and the active intervention by the central bank last week, most people think the yuan has only limited upward potential in the short term," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move below the 8.2920 level on Tuesday.
The yuan closed almost unchanged at 6.6460 from 6.6500 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at an intra-day low of 1.0706 from 1.0705 against the Hong Kong dollar.
